answer: To mitigate fake-identity attacks, decentralized networks employ the "comet" protocol, which utilizes a variant of digital signatures to verify agent identities. Each agent's public key is linked to a unique, publicly accessible "pigment" - a cryptographic hash of their underlying identity. If an attacker attempts to create multiple identities, their new keys will be distinct and incompatible with the existing "jetty" of public keys, rendering them distinguishable and invalid.
